editorial:
Imagine a TV network so desperate for viewers that they literally throw their boss out the window. That is exactly how things kick off here, and it sets a wild tone for the rest of the ride. You get to see Bugs Bunny step into the corporate world as the new president of QTTV because the executives think a cartoon rabbit is the only one who actually knows how to entertain people. The vibe is light, zany, and full of that classic Looney Tunes energy that makes you feel like a kid again. It is a funny look at how the TV industry works, wrapped in a package of slapstick humor and clever jokes.

, keeping the pace moving quickly so you never get bored. The voice acting is spot on, and the animation feels cozy and nostalgic. If you are looking for a stress-free movie to watch with the family, this is a great pick. It is a simple, joyful watch that does not take itself too seriously.
endingExplained: After causing plenty of chaos at the network, Bugs realizes that running a TV station is a lot more work than just making cartoons. The story wraps up with Bugs using his wit to fix the ratings while staying true to his mischievous nature. He eventually steps back from the corporate stress, proving that he is much better at being a star than a boss. Everything ends with a big laugh and a nod to the golden age of animation.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Looney Tunes and goofy humor.
